title: The Discount That Ate the Profit
kicker: A data story · one retailer · 9,994 orders · 2015–2018
subtitle: Sales grew every year. Profit barely did — and the discounts explain why.
sourceNote: Source: the public 'Sample – Superstore' dataset (fictional US retailer). Every number on this page is computed from it.

defaults.subtitle: Total profit 2015–2018 and margin (profit ÷ sales)

steps.heading: Four years, $2.3 million in sales.
steps.text: 9,994 order lines from a US office-supplies retailer, 2015–2018.

steps.heading: …and $286,000 in profit.
steps.text: A 12.5% margin. Not bad for retail — but look where it comes from.

steps.heading: Sales grew every year.
steps.text: From $484k in 2015 to $733k in 2018 — up 51%. Three categories of roughly equal size, all growing.

steps.heading: Roughly a third each.
steps.text: Furniture, Office Supplies and Technology each bring in about a third of revenue, month after month.

state.subtitle: Share of monthly sales by category

steps.heading: But not a third of the profit.
steps.text: Technology and Office Supplies each earn about 17 cents on the dollar. Furniture earns 2.5 cents — $18k of profit on $742k of sales.

steps.heading: Every dollar of profit came from orders that weren't discounted.
steps.text: Undiscounted orders made $321k. Discounted orders — more than half of all lines — lost $35k in total.

steps.heading: Small discounts are fine. Big ones aren't.
steps.text: 10–20% off still earns 12–13%. From 30% off upwards, every band loses money — 70–80% off loses more than it sells.

steps.heading: The more a product is discounted, the less it earns.
steps.text: Each circle is a sub-category. Paper and Labels are barely discounted and earn 40%+; Tables average 26% off and lose 8.6%.

steps.heading: Furniture's problem is Tables.
steps.text: Tables: $207k in sales, −$17.7k profit, average discount 26%. Bookcases lose too. Chairs and Furnishings carry the category.

steps.heading: It also has an address.
steps.text: New York and California make the money. Texas lost $25.7k, Ohio $17.0k, Pennsylvania $15.6k and Illinois $12.6k — four states in the red.

steps.heading: Central drags.
steps.text: West and East earn 14–15%. The Central region — Texas, Illinois — earns 7.9%.

steps.heading: So what would you change?
steps.text: Cap discounts below 30%, fix or drop Tables, and look hard at Texas — the data says that's where the profit went.

footerHtml: Data: the public Sample – Superstore dataset (a fictional US retailer used in Tableau tutorials), copy from github.com/leonism/sample-superstore. That copy contains 806 malformed rows and 799 duplicated Row IDs; both were removed, leaving the canonical 9,994 order lines (2015–2018). Sales and profit are nominal dollars per order line; discount is a fraction of list price; margin = profit ÷ sales. Discount bands: 0%, 10–15%, 20%, 30–45%, 50–60%, 70–80%.
